name: alfred-code
check_batch: run the tests that cover the change and `npm run lint`
not_for: Not for a consuming project, which runs the stack's `task-solve`; not for a release, which has its own procedure.
settled: A design already settled by a run order or the user's rulings skips the spec and goes to the plan.
checks: - per batch: `npm run lint` and the tests that cover the change;
- a temp-project matrix from this working tree with CLAUDE.md's required edge cases - fresh install, update over
an older install, re-run, the user's own config kept, missing or garbage input, every scope, every boundary -
reading the written files, never the exit code alone;
- the full `npm test` once, in the background, its output to a log, its tail read.
not_here: - The stack's own `task-solve` and its seats, stamps and stops.

notes: The shipped skills live in stack/skills; this repo's own .claude/skills (the repo-audit family, plugin-authoring and the other synced authoring skills) is outside the shipped catalog, is audited only when the user names it, and npm run lint does not hold it.

The multi-home registry is meta/shared-rules.json at the repo root: one entry per multi-home rule, the canonical owner plus every restatement site pinned by a marker phrase; npm run lint fails when a copy drifts, and any pass that adds, moves or rewords multi-home text updates it in the same pass.

The install catalogs are meta/recommendations.json (seeds skills per stack profile) and meta/stack-graph.json (pulls; npm run graph rewrites it); a skill unreachable from any seed is optional, and a named load directive of an optional skill is a coupling defect.
The optional-cite checks in scripts/lint-skills.js (lintOptionalCites, run by npm run lint) flag a named load directive of a skill an install can lack; they must be green.
Lint check 15c caps each skill description plus when_to_use at 160 chars (since 2.1.2), and check 15 caps any description at 1,000.
Lint check 33 prints the always-on budget every run: skill descriptions, pathless rules and agent descriptions summed under 80,000 chars - quote it under Dimension 3.
Skills trigger mainly through the convention rules in stack/rules, which tell the model to call the skill (the rule-forced trigger path).

Offline step grader: where meta/skill-comply/<skill>/expect.json exists, node scripts/skill-comply.js grade scores a transcript step by step offline; its replay --live is a billed nested session the user must approve first, and compare applies the A/B ship rule over two replay outputs.
Every stack skill is installed as a project copy (since 2.1.0), so the skillOverrides visibility override reaches it for the with/without evaluation.

No plugin carries a stack skill (since 2.1.0), so claude plugin eval cannot see them directly: npm run eval-bundle -- <out> builds one plugin holding the core and the whole library; meta/evals/library/ holds one case per stack profile graded arm: both; the run is billed.

The session analyzer is the capture-usage-report skill (stack/skills/capture-usage-report): its SKILLS table and scorecard give per-skill activation counts per session - record the pre-edit numbers beside an edit.
The catalog names skills as noun phrases (dotnet-testing), not gerunds; keep new names consistent.

Measured history of this catalog: before the 2.1.2 cap angular-testing and ts-js-testing shared 35 trigger terms (Jaccard 0.44) and the architecture and coverage loops 0.35; 21 descriptions carried a 'Triggers on' clause before 2.1.2 and none did on 2026-09-29; before the cap 61 of 79 descriptions had no 'use' or 'when' in their first 250 chars and descriptions averaged ~190 tokens (60k chars over 79 skills).

Measured on 2026-09-29: 89 skills, none using allowed-tools or disallowed-tools; descriptions 13,586 chars total (~153 chars, ~40 tokens each); 24 bodies over 12k chars and 2 over 20k; the reference layer held 193 files (an earlier 146-file layer had 4 reachable only through a sibling); no skill directory held a human-centric file (README, CHANGELOG).

The skill catalog is stack/skills and the rule catalog stack/rules; agents cite rules by deployed path (.claude/rules/...) while existence is checked against stack/rules; the CLAUDE.md template agents are judged against is stack/AGENTS.template.md; the repo's root CLAUDE.md is its own working file and is out of scope.

Seat delivery (since 2.1.0): all seats (44-45) ride the core plugin, and each seat a project's selection did not pick is denied per project as Agent(alfred-code:<seat>); the full copy route copies the picked seats into .claude/agents instead.

A seat and its frontmatter preloads seed together; skills: preloads are BARE names that resolve to the project's library copies, and a seat whose preloaded skills were not copied is never picked; an always-on (cross-cutting) seat can count on nothing stack-specific.

Preload spelling: lint check 50 fails a skills: preload spelled alfred-code:<skill> instead of bare; npm run scope-preloads (node scripts/scope-agent-preloads.js --write) rewrites every preload to the spelling its placement needs.

Dispatch spelling: a plugin seat answers only to alfred-code:<seat> (a bare name returns 'Agent type not found'); every body that dispatches a seat keeps that roster spelling, pinned by scripts/seat-dispatch-spelling.test.js.
MCP tool spelling in tools: grants is mcp__plugin_<server>_<server>__ (plugin and server share the name); lint check 54 fails a bare mcp__<server>__ spelling.

Install decisions: what a project needs is proven by meta/evidence.json against the project's own manifests or seeded per stack in meta/recommendations.json, with meta/stack-graph.json pulls; the optional-cite checks in npm run lint cover the skill half and must be green, MCP cites are audited by hand.
The suggests: frontmatter is removed and must not return: it offered dotnet-aspire to a project with no Aspire and angular-security to a WinForms one; a described cite gets no install edge.

The multi-home registry is meta/shared-rules.json (owner plus marker-pinned sites; npm run lint fails on a drifted copy); a registry-synced rule keeps its copies inline without naming the sibling artifacts.
A renamed or retired seat gets its retired.agents and renamed.agents rows in meta/stack-manifest.json (the one home of a changed shipped name).

Dispatch is explicit-only (the capabilities rule and the dispatch guard stack/hooks/guard-unapproved-dispatch.js, a PreToolUse guard on Task|Agent), so a 'Use PROACTIVELY' cue in a seat description is a defect.
Lint check 15b caps an agent description at 300 chars: the 'Use when...' sentence and its 'Do NOT use' clause, with the rest of the scope in the agent's ## Scope body section.

An install unit is the cross-cutting seats plus one stack's vertical; measured 2026-09-29 after the 300-char cap, a single-stack install's seeded seats are 12-14 at ~3.4k-4.0k chars (~1k tokens), all 44 sum 12,750 chars (~3.2k tokens, re-measured 2026-10-20) - also what a repo the stack never set up lists, since no deny is written there (the 2.1.0 known ceiling); before the cap 16 seats carried ~13.8k chars and 43 seats 38k.
Measured preload cost: 26k-70k chars per designer / implementer / verifier seat.
This stack's verifier seats route over-build to a punch list and never block on it.

The session analyzer is the capture-usage-report skill: its SUBAGENTS table and dispatch-overhead row are the observable for a seat edit - record preload share, output per dispatch and status words returned before the edit.
Rule sources live in stack/rules/ and hook sources in stack/hooks/ (the audit.hooks roots); audit the sources but reason about loading, paths globs and cross-file references in the deployed layout.

The installer is node scripts/install/alfred-code.js (one installer, every OS); it deploys each rule as a library copy in the target project's .claude/rules/, its hash recorded in the install stamp, with drift and staleness reported by scripts/library-check.js.
Confirm the source-to-deployed mapping from meta/stack-manifest.json (the six lists the installer reads) and the installer's own scripts/install/ modules, never by assumption.
stack/rules/alfred-docs-root.md carries the __DOCS_ROOT__ placeholder the installer stamps on every run, so its deployed text is not the source's text.

The GENERATED rules alfred-awareness.md and project-code-style.md are written by the capture skill that owns each one, which fixes their shape; a finding there lands in that skill, never in a hand edit of the rule.

The CLAUDE.md template read for the conflict and duplication maps is stack/AGENTS.template.md; the repo-root CLAUDE.md is this repo's own working file, read for context only and never scored or edited.

The compaction instructions (what the summary keeps verbatim) are owned by the always-on navigation baseline rule stack/rules/alfred-navigation.md; any other always-on file restating them is a duplicate.

Lint check 33 (scripts/always-on-surface.js, run by npm run lint) caps the shipped always-on surface at 80,000 chars: the pathless alfred-*.md rules as injected, every agent description with its (Tools: ...) suffix, every model-invocable skill description plus when_to_use, and the generated capabilities rule's fixed text; /alfred-code:status reports each install's floor.
An always-on rule may name only what every install gets; the symbol-navigation server the baseline locks is the one MCP server every project is guaranteed.

What each rule's install unit guarantees is read from meta/recommendations.json (seeds) and meta/stack-graph.json (pulls, regenerated by npm run graph); lint checks 25 and 26 in npm run lint are the optional-cite checks covering the skill half and must be green, while MCP cites are audited by hand.

The multi-home registry is meta/shared-rules.json: one entry per multi-home rule naming the canonical owner and every restatement site, each pinned by a marker phrase; lint check 24 fails when a copy's marker drifts, and any pass that adds, moves or rewords multi-home text updates the registry in the same pass.
Measured build-directory reads cost ~8.6k tokens across 115 sessions, so a permissions.deny Read() entry for build and vendored trees is recorded as available, not owed.

Previous always-on measurement to compare against: the seven always-on rules measured 170 non-empty lines, 25,082 chars (~6.3k tokens) and 92 bullets on 2026-09-29, before the project CLAUDE.md and the descriptions are added; the earlier six-rule set counted ~220 directive sentences with 48 zero-exception lines.
The rules' 'measured:' clauses are the consequence clause of the imperative-consequence-mechanism shape: keep the one that carries the reason and cut a second number that restates it.
The adherence observables are the usage analyzer's scorecard rows (scripts/analyze-usage.js) and the hook-blocks ledger; record their pre-edit numbers beside each edit.
Hook wiring is the hooks list in meta/stack-manifest.json: a row's matcher is a PreToolUse matcher, or @Event / @Event:matcher for any other event.

scripts/build-marketplace.js (mergeHooks) folds the manifest's hooks rows into the core alfred-code entry's inline hooks block in meta/plugin-entries.json and then the root plugin manifest, after the core's own inline entries (guard-layer-table.js and library-stamp.js in setup-plugin/hooks/, which are house hooks too); npm run plugin-manifest regenerates it, and lint checks 48 and 49 hold the core hooks block to the manifest's wiring table.

Hook timeouts live in the HOOK_TIMEOUTS table in scripts/install/settings.js, read by both the core-entry generator and the copy-route writer: 10 seconds by default (every hook measured under 30 ms), 60 on the Stop entries of check-turn-build.js and history-session.js, and the shell-guards.js dispatcher gets the sum of its guards' 10 s; the comment above HOOK_TIMEOUTS carries the measured spawn time.

scripts/install/settings.js also wires the hooks into a project's settings.json on the copy route (ALFRED_CODE_HOOKS_VIA_PLUGIN=false); on the default plugin route a deployed settings.json carries no stack hook entry, only ALFRED_CODE_HOOKS_OFF naming the hooks the walk did not pick, so any stack hook entry there is a leftover.

The hook retirement list is retired.hooks in meta/stack-manifest.json; update prunes the retired set from a deployed settings.json, the HTML and README hook counts must agree with the manifest, and the env-gated instrument hook (instrument-tool-usage.js) is wired off by default.
Child hooks to audit come from every plugin in the plugins list of meta/stack-manifest.json.
Hooks are read against the root layers stack/rules, stack/skills and stack/agents.

The guard-block ledger is <data root>/statistics/hook-blocks/<session>.jsonl under each audited project's generated-docs root, one row per block (timestamp, hook, event, tool, reason); node scripts/analyze-usage.js <corpus> --hook-blocks <dir> reads the per-hook block rate with its denominator.

The ten `Bash|PowerShell|Monitor` PreToolUse guards listed at the top of shell-guards.js are wired as ONE shell-guards.js hook that runs each guard in-process, and the seven file-tool guards in file-guards.js the same way; each guard keeps its own gates and ledger row, and a throwing guard fails open alone.
Every hook is wired in exec form: node with ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/<file> as its first argument, with no shell and no quoting.

Shared hook code has one home each in stack/hooks: hook-prelude.js holds the gates (the csv opt-out, the hook_profile userConfig, the stand-down beside a still-wired copied twin, a repo never set up, a Cursor host), fresh-session.js the fresh-session arithmetic, shell-writes.js the shell-write parse, hidden-chars.js the hidden-character class; a hook requires them from its own directory and never inlines them.
A regex several hooks still carry inline (the Git Bash mount path) is pinned as a shared rule with marker-pinned copies in meta/shared-rules.json.
A user-facing gate ends in ONE AskUserQuestion whose answer is honoured through a session-own, expiring receipt under <data root>/state/.
The Cursor twin repo ships a hook layer of its own: a hook protocol change here is written to a task card for that repo.
The stack installs to Windows, so a guard's tests replay its failure shape on the PowerShell route too.
Measured cold p50 latency (audit 2026-10-14): a bare node start 23.8 ms, a single hook 26-52 ms, the shell-guards.js dispatcher 58.7-209.9 ms - re-measure per machine.

stack/AGENTS.template.md is seeded as `.claude/AGENTS.md` by node scripts/install/alfred-code.js (a root AGENTS.md on --instructions-at root), and only into a project that has no AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

Rule links in the template use the deployed paths (.claude/rules/...), while their existence is checked against the source catalog at stack/rules; confirm the mapping from meta/stack-manifest.json and the installer's scripts/install/ modules.

Filling or improving one project's CLAUDE.md (create, or improve with every change shown first) belongs to the fill skill stack/skills/habits-adjust-agents-md/; an audit finding about how files get filled lands in that skill, not in the template.

The filled-file checker is node scripts/agents-md-check.js --file <path> (read-only, no model call): it checks the named paths, each command's program on PATH or in the project, leftover placeholders, TODOs and template text; --list names the files it would check and marks an untouched seed; its rows are heuristic, so read each one before acting on it.
The repo-root CLAUDE.md is this repo's own working file: read it for context, never score or edit it.

Lint check 33 (scripts/always-on-surface.js, run by npm run lint) caps the shipped always-on baseline at 80,000 chars: the pathless rules as injected, every skill and agent description, the seats' tools lists and the generated capabilities rule's fixed text; /alfred-code:status reports each install's floor.

Since 2.10.1 alfred-code leaves auto memory as it is (its memory server and alfred-memory.md are retired, and the first update past them lifts the switch-off an earlier release wrote), so in an installed project auto memory is the corrections-and-preferences store.
The compaction-instructions line is carried by the always-on navigation baseline rule alfred-navigation.md, so a project CLAUDE.md that restates it is a duplicate.
The always-on baseline every install carries is the alfred-*.md rules; a template pointer may name those, and anything beyond them is described rather than named.

The template keeps no rules table since 2026-10-21 (the user's ruling: every rule file in .claude/rules/ loads itself, so a list only repeats them each session); Dimension 2's governing-rules item is scored on the template's 'List no rules here' line, and a template that lists rules deducts.

What every install guarantees is read from meta/recommendations.json (seeds) and meta/stack-graph.json (pulls); lint checks 25 and 26 in npm run lint are the optional-cite checks and must be green, while MCP cites are audited by hand.

Template outline history to compare against: measured 2026-11-03 at 1 live line (its H1, 18 chars) with the outline in comment blocks; 2026-09-29 it was 22 live lines, 3,165 chars; the outline carries the forbid-list (item 7) and the domain-terms map (item 1) and its architecture item rules out the folder tour, where an earlier 19-line version had neither item and asked for 'folder organization'.
The template's 'Load by artifact' table (item 13) is its implementation of the hub-and-spoke form scored under Dimension 1's nested-files item.

The adherence observables are the analyzer scorecard rows (scripts/analyze-usage.js: compaction re-reads, long answers, green claims, checked commits) and the hook-blocks ledger; record their pre-edit numbers beside each edit.

The install list is the plugins list in meta/stack-manifest.json, read by the Node seed scripts/install/alfred-code.js, the one installer route (the shell twins are deleted); the *-lsp pair is suggested on evidence and claude-hud is optional.
The stack's own plugin manifest lists no MCP server since 2.10.1.

The envoydev marketplace lives in envoydev/plugins-marketplaces since 2026-11-14 and also lists alfred-mods and alfred-tools, which the stack never installs or updates (the user's ruling of 2026-10-27): their packaging is /repo-audit-system's, and each is scored here only where the audited registry shows it installed.

The guided-install catalogs are meta/recommendations.json (the always seeds, per-stack plugins seeds, opt-in in general), meta/plugin-settings.json (one row per plugin with its verified version), meta/stack-graph.json (regenerated by npm run graph) and meta/retired-plugins.json.
The plugin retirement path is the manifest's retired.plugins plus a meta/retired-plugins.json row (retiredIn, addBack) that update uninstalls by its full spec.
The install list is restated in the HTML plugins table and the README count, and npm run lint holds the manifest to both.

Usage is measured by node scripts/analyze-usage.js <CORPUS> - its INVENTORY vs USE block scores each installed plugin per session and per corpus with a how column; pass --plugins <registry> when the corpus came from another machine.
The install-side cost floor is the stack's own /alfred-code:status line.

The always-on house rules are the alfred-*.md set; the capabilities rule makes agent dispatch explicit-only, so a child agent's proactive cues are a finding, and side-effect skills fall under the house side-effect gate.
Plugins are a Claude-only surface: the Cursor twin repo ships none, so the two-repo mirror discipline does not apply to the PLUGINS block.

The LSP pair ships no plugin.json (declared wholly in its marketplace entry), so the 2026-11-03 rule that entry mcpServers/lspServers/userConfig/channels do not apply beside a plugin.json leaves it untouched.
The stack's own plugin splits commands from skills on purpose, for display, and that split stands despite the docs preferring skills.
For a plugin replaced by a house hook, verify through the <data root>/statistics/hook-blocks/ ledger row of the replacement hook.
Child plugins are read against the root layers stack/rules, stack/skills, stack/agents and stack/hooks.
Agents are called seats in this repo; the audit's 'agent' means a seat.

PROFILES are listed by `node scripts/profile-fixture.js --help`: every `stacks` key of `meta/recommendations.json` plus `bare`; a key with no markers fails its test, and each profile's marker files are the script's `MARKERS`.

The fixture tool is `node scripts/profile-fixture.js <profile> <WORKDIR>`: it exports the tree once, registers the export as the stack's marketplace on an isolated account dir (through a one-entry stand-in catalog it writes into the export), installs the always seed plus the profile's selection as setup would accept, and prints the map command.
The fixture clean step is `node scripts/profile-fixture.js --clean <WORKDIR>`, which removes only what the fixture script writes and prints `removed:` and `left:`.

The session-surface tool is `HOME=<home> node scripts/session-surface.js <project> --config-dir <account> --run-hooks --listing-fraction <f> --window <WINDOW> --json`; its JSON prints no machine path, and exit 1 means a hook wrote outside the project (a S4 finding with the path).
`scripts/session-surface.js` leaves `session-surface-*` folders in the OS temp dir; the cleanup proves none remain with `find <tmp> -maxdepth 1 -name 'session-surface-*'`.

`scripts/session-surface.js` encodes currency rows and its comments name the page each came from: a DRIFTED row is corrected there too; it reads `skillListingMaxDescChars` from the fixture's settings with `LISTING_MAX_DESC` as the fallback, and models only the default Project instructions value (`AGENTS_FILES`).
The session-surface map's owner split for session-start chars is house / generated / plugin.
RESULTS default to `<docs-path>/audits/<YYYY-MM-DD>/system/`, where the docs root is always `<data root>/docs` (`.alfred/docs` by default); machine-local, never committed.

OWN_PLUGIN_ROOT is the core `alfred-code` entry, generated into `./meta/plugin-entries.json` by `scripts/build-marketplace.js` and written to the root `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` by `npm run plugin-manifest`; `./setup-plugin` holds its commands, its router skill, its own hooks, its eval cases and the `plugin.json` whose `version` the release tags.
No MCP entry ships since 2.10.1: `stack/mcp/shipped-mcps.json` is the record, so a server row in the core manifest is a finding.
The marketplace catalog lives in envoydev/plugins-marketplaces since 2026-11-14; this repo ships no marketplace.json and lint check 49 fails one at the root.
The `claude plugin eval` suite for the own plugin is `setup-plugin/evals/`; run it with and without where a fix touched a command or the router skill.

The install proof for every shipped file a fix changed is the temp-project matrix in the repo `CLAUDE.md`: fresh, update over the last release, re-run, the user's own config kept, malformed input, every scope touched.
The awareness checklist's navigation order is: a symbol through the `LSP` tool, then a scoped grep, never a whole-file read; a vendor's page through `WebFetch` (no MCP server ships since 2.10.1).

The house do-nots a first turn can break are: commit only on the user's word, no whole-file read, no secret read by value; a missing whole-file-read do-not costs as much in S5 as the commit and secret ones.

A fresh install has no awareness docs, awareness rule or architecture rule until `/alfred-code:init` writes them through the capture skills; read what each will state from `stack/skills/capture-awareness/references/agents.md`, `project.md` and `related-projects.md`, the rule's copy target in its `SKILL.md`, and the other `.claude/rules/<name>.md` targets the map lists as `generated`.
The stack seeds an AGENTS.md; its directives are swept against skills, seats and hook injections in the conflict map.
The corpus analyzer is `node scripts/analyze-usage.js <CORPUS>`.
The hook-block ledger is `<data root>/statistics/hook-blocks/*.jsonl` (the docs root's `hook-blocks/` before 2.8.0).
Lint check 33 holds the repo's catalog; the system audit measures what one install holds instead.
The listing-budget measurement: the repo CLAUDE.md records '39 skills, 19901 chars > 8000 budget' at a 200K window and the `0.01` default on Claude Code 2.1.284.

The denied-seat evidence is spike S3 in `docs/plugin-migration-evidence.md`, re-measured 2026-10-16 on 2.1.301 in an aspnet install of 2.5.0: the Agent tool listed 21 seats with none of the 23 denied, while `/context`'s 'Custom agents' row still counted all 44 definitions.
The bare-MCP-tool-name deny behaviour is also recorded in `.claude/rules/repo-installer.md`.

Renames: no `renames` key (it strands an install - `docs/plugin-cli-evidence.md` S11, S16; lint check 49 fails on one); the old id stays LISTED as a retired alias carrying its successor (an unlisted entry still enabled silently stops loading, S25) until evidence shows no install resolves through it.
The own plugin's display-driven split is a measured choice: commands that list namespaced-only and a router skill that lists bare; never convert either to gain a component-fit point.
The root declares its children in one place the lint reads, and the component frontmatter is proven by the repo's lint (`npm run lint`).

The collection root is globbed as `docs/*investigation*/` (gitignored by that pattern); the default name is `docs/session-investigation/`, but the real collection sits in `docs/sessions-investigation/`.

The per-project report skill is the stack's `capture-usage-report` (`/capture-usage-report`), run in a fresh session inside the project; it fills the authored judgment sections and owns the report-generation prompt, so a NOT-STACK finding about a bundle's report routes its durable half there.

The analyzer is `node scripts/analyze-usage.js`: it dedupes usage by message id and finds a bundle's sibling `subagents/` itself; it writes with `--out <file>` (never a `>` redirect, which the permission classifier denies); `--json` gives `analyzer.json`, plain gives `analyzer-full.txt`, `--report-md` gives the skeleton `report-usage.md`.

The analyzer's rollup leaves out the live session (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`); `--exclude-session <id>` drops another; `--docs-root <root>` names a non-default docs path; it reads the ledgers beside a bundle copy itself.

The collector is `node scripts/collect-session.js <transcript> --out <folder>` (`--data-root <folder>` names an older install's data root); it writes the transcript, `subagents/`, `collected.json` (the receipt), `context.json`, `context/`, both ledgers beside the copy and under `data/`, the session's state, its docs and hook temp files.

Bundle file names: `session.jsonl` or `<session-id>.jsonl`; `tool-usage-<sid>.jsonl` (tool ledger); `hook-blocks-<sid>.jsonl` (guard blocks); `collected.json` (receipt, printed in reports as `## Evidence coverage`); `context.json` and `context/` (roots, variables, plugins, the instrument switch, the install stamp, workspace record and session-inspector status); `data/` (the data-root mirror); `docs/`, `tmp/`; `analyzer.json` / `analysis.json` / `analyzer-full.txt`; `report-usage.md`.
Each collected project directory also carries `statistics/tools-usage/<session-id>.jsonl` and `statistics/hook-blocks/<session-id>.jsonl`, the authority when a bundle's own copy is missing.

Route 1 copies `SUMMARY.md`, `_rollup.txt` (as `rollup.txt`) and every session folder out of `<project>/<data root>/statistics/usage-report/`, where the data root is `.alfred`; an install not updated to 2.8.0 keeps `usage-report/` (or `alfred-code-usage-report/` before 2.1.7) under its docs root: a leftover `ALFRED_CODE_DOCS_PATH` wins, else `<data root>/docs` (`.claude/docs` before 2.0.0).
An older bundle with no `collected.json` gets its two ledgers from the data root's `statistics/` (`tools-usage/<sid>.jsonl`, `hook-blocks/<sid>.jsonl`; the docs root before 2.8.0).
The collection root being git-ignored is what lets the collector's gate copy the text stores.
The flow-skill families judged under load are `/task-*`, `/loop-*`, `/capture-*` and `/issue-*`.

The analyzer's EFFICIENCY block is carried in `--json` as `main.efficiency` plus `dispatchOverhead`; each row is opened per `stack/skills/capture-usage-report/references/diagnosis-discipline.md` before it is costed.
Path-rule attachment is read by the analyzer's `Inventory vs use` section from two records: the harness's `nested_memory` attach row and `guard-read-whole-file.js`'s shell-route notice.

The inventory is the analyzer's `Inventory vs use` section (`inventory` in `--json`); a row sourced `catalog` means the project's installed set was not reachable - re-run with `--inventory <that project's .claude>` before filing a non-use finding; one recursive run over the collection root gives `installed in K of M sessions, used in N` per name.
Report integrity: `node scripts/analyze-usage.js --check-report <report-usage.md>` prints every judgment number that cites no machine row of that same report.
Conformance: the skeleton's `## Conformance - expected vs observed (machine-written)` section grades each claim in `meta/conformance.json` and every `meta/skill-comply/` step over the session.

The generated docs a session should read for orientation are `<docs-path>/awareness/ARCHITECTURE-AWARENESS.md` and its `references/`, `quality/ARCHITECTURE-ASSESSMENT.md`, `preferences/PROJECT-CODE-PREFERENCES.md`, and the test-coverage capture.
The stack ships a correction-streak hook; the effectiveness verdict says whether its streak threshold would have met the session's corrections.
Synthesis honours the repo's invariants: platform-neutral skill bodies and the shared-rules registry for multi-home text.
An applied fix cites the session evidence (bundle id and measured number) in its commit, as the prove-don't-assert rule demands.
